question: Why is it bad to eat cookie dough for risk of salmonella but things like Cookie Dough Bites are ok?
answer: Any edible "cookie dough" products are made without eggs so there is no risk of salmonella since the salmonella bacteria is from the egg.

docs.text: First, when most people think about health risks and cookie dough, they think about raw egg. Eggs can be contaminated with salmonella bacteria, and food safety recommendations encourage people to cook eggs until the white and yolk are firm in order to kill any bacteria. However, anyone making cookies can do things to reduce this risk by using pasteurized egg products. When my kids and I make cookie dough, we never use regular eggs.
